title: Automating Tests and AI-Assisted Verification
code: # AI Agent Project Context: Health Economic Model Verification  ## 1. Persona & Scope You are an expert Health Economist and R Software Developer. Your goal is to write robust, transparent, and reproducible unit tests for HTA models using the `testthat` package.  ## 2. Structural Contract: Helper Functions To ensure modularity and "separation of concerns," all model interactions must follow these interface patterns:  * **Required Setters/Mutators** (Must return input object):   * `set_discount_rate(input, discount_rate)`   * `set_costs(input, scenario, values)`   * `set_p_matrix(input, scenario, values)`   * `set_utilities(input, scenario, values)`   * `set_time_horizon(input, scenario, values)`  * **Required Getters/Accessors**:   * `get_qalys(res)`: Extract total QALYs.   * `get_costs(res)`: Extract total costs.   * `get_le(res)`: Extract life expectancy.   * `get_icer(res)`: Extract ICER.  * **Required Wrappers & Utilities**:   * `run_model(data, ...)`: Mandatory wrapper.   * `compare_model_runs(...)`: Encapsulate comparison logic for different model outputs.  ## 3. Test Registry (Source of Truth) All automated verification must align with these:  | ID  | Group | Test Condition                 | Expected Result           | |-----|-------|--------------------------------|---------------------------| | T01 | Pop   | Set relative effects = 1       | Equal LYGs & QALYs        | | T02 | Pop   | Set mortality = 0              | LE = time horizon         | | T03 | Pop   | Set mortality = 1              | LE = 1                    | | T04 | QALY  | Set discount rate = 0 (u=1)    | Total QALYs = LE          | | T05 | QALY  | Set utilities = 1              | QALY gains = LYGS         | | T06 | QALY  | Positive discount rate         | Disc QALYs < Undisc       | | T07 | QALY  | QALY discount rate = inf       | QALYs t>0 -> 0            | | T08 | Cost  | Set intervention costs = 0     | ICER is reduced           | | T09 | Cost  | Increase intervention costs    | ICER is increased         | | T10 | Cost  | Set cost discount rate = 0     | Disc costs = Undisc       | | T11 | Cost  | Set cost discount rate = inf   | Costs t>0 -> 0            | | T12 | Input | Sampled parameters             | Bounds (e.g. 0-1)         |  ## 4. Coding Standard & Implementation Rules * **Modular Architecture**: "Separation of concerns" is mandatory. Do not write monolithic scripts. * **TDD**: Define expectations based on requirements before writing model functions. * **Naming**: Every `test_that()` block must start with its Registry ID. * **Tolerance**: Use `tolerance = 0.01` for floating-point comparisons.

title: Automating Tests and AI-Assisted Verification
text: Modellers must remain vigilant three failure modes using AI assistants: Semantically Inverted Logic: LLM may generate syntactically valid code inverts intended inequality (e.g., asserting discounted costs greater undiscounted costs). False Sense Completeness: LLM know clinical assumptions model-specific versus universal. Unreviewed Code: Every generated test must read understood modeller committed. Two software testing paradigms particularly effective mitigating AI-induced errors: Smoke Testing: preliminary check executes model pipeline AI-generated inputs parameter structures verify model runs completion without fatal errors NaNs investing time deeper validation. Regression Testing: Running comprehensive T01 – T12 test suite AI-assisted refactoring feature addition verify new edits silently broken previously verified baseline model logic.

what: Test T06: Discounted QALYs Are Strictly Lower Than Undiscounted QALYs
title: R Test Code Examples
text: verify applying standard positive discount rate (r=3.5%r = 3.5\%) results strictly lower total QALYs compared undiscounted run (r=0%r = 0\%) treatment scenarios (s=1,2s = 1, 2): Step 1: Run model discount rate r=0%r = 0\% (undiscounted). Step 2: Run model discount rate r=3.5%r = 3.5\% (discounted). Step 3: Assert qPVs(r=3.5%)<qPVs(r=0%)q^s_{PV}(r = 3.5\%) < q^s_{PV}(r = 0\%) treatment using expect_lt().
code: test_that("T06: Discounted QALYs are lower than undiscounted QALYs", {   # run model with standard discounting (3.5%)   results_discounted <- with(     base_params,     ce_markov(       start_pop, p_matrix, state_c_matrix,       state_q_matrix, n_cycles,       discount_rate = 0.035     )   )    # run model with NO discounting (0%)   results_undiscounted <- with(     base_params,     ce_markov(       start_pop, p_matrix, state_c_matrix,       state_q_matrix, n_cycles,       discount_rate = 0.0     )   )    # alternatively, using the run_model() wrapper:   # results_discounted <- run_model(base_params, discount_rate = 0.035)   # results_undiscounted <- run_model(base_params, discount_rate = 0.00)    # extract the total QALYs using getter   qaly_discounted <- get_qalys(results_discounted)   qaly_undiscounted <- get_qalys(results_undiscounted)    # expectation: discounted must be less than undiscounted value   expect_lt(     qaly_discounted["without_drug"],     qaly_undiscounted["without_drug"]   )   expect_lt(     qaly_discounted["with_drug"],     qaly_undiscounted["with_drug"]   ) }) #> Test passed with 2 successes 🥇.

what: Tests T07 & T11: High Discounting Reduces Future Value to Zero
title: R Test Code Examples
text: arbitrarily large discount rate (r→∞r \\infty), costs QALYs incurred initial cycle (t>0t > 0) converge zero, total outcomes across full time horizon equal outcomes cycle 0 alone (n_cycles = 1). check depends numerical convergence, use tolerance argument expect_equal(). use discount_rate = 1000 instead Inf? Inf mathematically ideal, arbitrarily large finite number (1000) recommended practice test code remains generalizable computationally stable adapted downstream numerical operations (optimization routines) may fail strictly infinite values.
code: test_that("T07 & T11: High discounting reduces future value to 0", {   # Run full model with extreme discount   res_high_disc <- run_model(base_params, discount_rate = 1000)    # Run a baseline model for only 1 cycle (time 0)   res_cycle_zero <- run_model(base_params, n_cycles = 1)    # Check Costs (T11)   expect_equal(     get_costs(res_high_disc),     get_costs(res_cycle_zero),     tolerance = 0.01,     label = "T11: High discount total costs equal cycle 0 costs"   )    # Check QALYs (T07)   expect_equal(     get_qalys(res_high_disc),     get_qalys(res_cycle_zero),     tolerance = 0.01,     label = "T07: High discount total QALYs equal cycle 0 QALYs"   ) }) #> Test passed with 2 successes 🎊.

title: R Test Code Examples
text: Tests unit costs utilities often evaluate boundary conditions specific cost utility components zeroed scaled. Test T08 evaluates boundary condition intervention cost removed setting with_drug state costs equal without_drug baseline costs: C2=C1 C^2 = C^1 Provided baseline Incremental Effects (IE\text{IE}) strictly positive (IE>0\text{IE} > 0), removing intervention cost must strictly reduce ICER. use testthat::skip_if_not() explicitly guard directional assumption:
code: test_that("T08: Zero intervention cost strictly reduces ICER", {   # Temporary wrapper to isolate intervention cost   run_with_intervention_cost <- function(c_int) {     temp_params <- base_params     temp_params$state_c_matrix["with_drug", "Asymptomatic"] <-       temp_params$state_c_matrix["without_drug", "Asymptomatic"] + c_int      run_model(temp_params)   }    # Run model with a standard positive intervention cost   res_base <- run_model(base_params)    # Run model with zero intervention cost   res_no_int <- run_with_intervention_cost(c_int = 0)    # extract ICERs   res_no_int_icer <- get_icer(res_no_int)   res_base_icer <- get_icer(res_base)    # extract baseline Incremental Effects (IE) to handle ICER directionality   base_qalys <- get_qalys(res_base)   res_base_ie <- unname(     base_qalys["with_drug"] - base_qalys["without_drug"]   )    # verify ICER directional change based on the sign of IE   # skip the rest of this block if assumption fails   testthat::skip_if_not(     res_base_ie > 0,     "Baseline incremental QALYs are <= 0. Skipping ICER directionality tests."   )    expect_lt(res_no_int_icer, res_base_icer) }) #> Test passed with 1 success 🌈.

title: R Test Code Examples
text: Transition matrix logic can verified forcing extreme mortality risks check life expectancy (T01, T02, T03). Test T03, set probability transitioning "Dead" 11 (100%100\%) immediately states: Ps=(001001001) P^s = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} Using named dimension "Dead" rather numeric column index keeps test readable self-documenting. within-cycle correction applied, per-person life expectancy (get_le_pp()) must equal exactly 11 cycle scenarios:
code: test_that("T03: Immediate mortality gives life expectancy of 1", {   # modify p_matrix to force death   dead_p_matrix <- base_params$p_matrix   dead_p_matrix[] <- 0   dead_p_matrix[, "Dead", ] <- 1 # all transitions go to Dead    res_death <- run_model(base_params, p_matrix = dead_p_matrix)   res_le <- get_le_pp(res_death)    # is per-person life expectancy for all scenarios = 1 cycle   expect_equal(unname(res_le), rep(1, length(res_le))) }) #> Test passed with 1 success 🎊.

title: Introduction to testhta
text: effectively implement automated verification using testthat, underlying R code written single monolithic script relies global variables. Instead, testhta separates computational pipeline three modular domains: Input Parameters (base_params): Transition matrices, cost vectors, utility weights, time horizon, discount rate isolated structured list individual tests can inject boundary values without contaminating global environment. Simulation Engine (ce_markov()): Accepts input parameters, executes matrix multiplication across specified time horizon, returns single list object containing cohort traces summary outputs. Helper Functions (Wrappers, Setters, Getters): Abstract away internal structure input output lists test scripts remain concise resilient future refactoring.

title: Introduction to testhta
text: convenience wrapper run_model(data, ...) merges base_params named parameter overrides passed via ... (using modifyList()) calls ce_markov():
code: # Run the model with baseline parameters results <- run_model(base_params) names(results) #>  [1] "pop"            "total_LE"       "total_LYs"      "total_LE_pp"    #>  [5] "total_LYs_pp"   "cycle_costs"    "cycle_QALYs"    "total_costs"    #>  [9] "total_QALYs"    "total_costs_pp" "total_QALYs_pp"

title: Introduction to testhta
text: testhta provides getter (accessor) functions extract targeted outputs model run without hard-coding list element names throughout test suite: get_qalys(res) / get_qalys_pp(res): Extract total cohort QALYs per-person QALYs. get_costs(res) / get_costs_pp(res): Extract total cohort costs per-person costs. get_le(res) / get_le_pp(res): Extract total cohort Life Expectancy per-person Life Expectancy (undiscounted life-years). get_icer(res): Calculate Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) comparing with_drug without_drug.
code: # Total cohort QALYs and per-person QALYs get_qalys(results) #> without_drug    with_drug  #>     8394.580     8981.496 get_qalys_pp(results) #> without_drug    with_drug  #>     8.394580     8.981496  # Total cohort Costs and per-person Costs get_costs(results) #> without_drug    with_drug  #>      1147099      4865536 get_costs_pp(results) #> without_drug    with_drug  #>     1147.099     4865.536  # Total and per-person Life Expectancy (LE) get_le(results) #> without_drug    with_drug  #>     12064.16     12683.32 get_le_pp(results) #> without_drug    with_drug  #>     12.06416     12.68332  # Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) get_icer(results) #> [1] 6335.546

text: Similarly, setter (mutator) functions safely modify specific parameter within base_params return updated parameter list, enabling clean pipelines base R pipe (|>): set_discount_rate(input, discount_rate) set_time_horizon(input, n_cycles) set_costs(input, scenario, values) set_utilities(input, scenario, values) set_p_matrix(input, scenario, values) example, evaluate model 0%0\% discount rate 10-cycle time horizon:
code: scenario_results <- base_params |>   set_discount_rate(0) |>   set_time_horizon(10) |>   run_model()  get_icer(scenario_results) #> [1] 11902.39

title: Custom Expectations and Advanced Testing
text: testhta exports custom expectation wrappers run model parameter overrides, extract relevant outcome, assert equality directional relationships via testthat: check_model_qalys(data, expected_qalys, ..., tolerance = NULL, label = NULL) check_model_costs(data, expected_costs, ..., tolerance = NULL, label = NULL) check_model_le(data, expected_le, ..., label = NULL) check_model_le_pp(data, expected_le, ..., label = NULL) compare_model_runs(extractor_fn, comparison_fn, params_1, params_2, data, label = NULL)

title: Custom Expectations and Advanced Testing
text: Using base_params custom expectation helpers , can express entire deterministic verification registry cleanly:

title: Custom Expectations and Advanced Testing
code: test_that("QALY calculations", {   # T04: Undiscounted QALYs (with u=1) should equal LE   # This is a dynamic check (comparing two different outputs from the same run),   # so it is clearest to write directly with expect_equal().   u_one_matrix <- base_params$state_q_matrix   u_one_matrix[, c("Asymptomatic", "Progressive")] <- 1    test_run_t04 <- run_model(     base_params,     discount_rate = 0,     state_q_matrix = u_one_matrix   )   expect_equal(     get_qalys(test_run_t04),     get_le(test_run_t04),     label = "T04: Undiscounted QALYs (with u=1) should equal LE"   )    # T05: QALY gains exactly equal LYGs   test_run_t05 <- run_model(     base_params,     discount_rate = 0,     state_q_matrix = u_one_matrix   )   expect_equal(     get_qalys(test_run_t05)["with_drug"] -       get_qalys(test_run_t05)["without_drug"],     get_le(test_run_t05)["with_drug"] -       get_le(test_run_t05)["without_drug"],     label = "T05: QALYs exactly equals LYGs when all utilities are 1"   )    # T06: QALYs with standard discount < undiscounted QALYs   compare_model_runs(     extractor_fn = get_qalys,     comparison_fn = expect_lt,     params_1 = list(discount_rate = 0.035),     params_2 = list(discount_rate = 0),     data = base_params,     label = "T06: Discounted should be less than undiscounted QALYs"   )    # T07: QALY gains after time 0 equal zero   res_cycle_zero <- run_model(base_params, n_cycles = 1)    check_model_qalys(     data = base_params,     discount_rate = 1000,     expected_qalys = get_qalys(res_cycle_zero),     tolerance = 0.01,     label = "T07: High discount total QALYs equal cycle 0 QALYs"   ) }) #> Test passed with 5 successes 🥇.

title: Custom Expectations and Advanced Testing
code: test_that("Cost calculations", {   # Calculate baseline incremental QALYs   base_res <- run_model(base_params)   base_qalys <- get_qalys(base_res)   inc_qalys <- unname(     base_qalys["with_drug"] - base_qalys["without_drug"]   )    # skip the rest of this block if assumption fails   testthat::skip_if_not(     inc_qalys > 0,     "Baseline incremental QALYs are <= 0. Skipping ICER directionality tests."   )    # T08: Set intervention costs = 0. ICER is reduced   # (Assuming baseline Incremental Effects are strictly positive)   c_mat_zero_int <- base_params$state_c_matrix   c_mat_zero_int["with_drug", "Asymptomatic"] <-     c_mat_zero_int["without_drug", "Asymptomatic"]    compare_model_runs(     extractor_fn = get_icer,     comparison_fn = expect_lt,     params_1 = list(state_c_matrix = c_mat_zero_int),     params_2 = list(),     data = base_params,     label = "T08: Intervention costs = 0 reduces ICER"   )    # T09: Increase intervention costs. ICER is increased   c_mat_high_int <- base_params$state_c_matrix   c_mat_high_int["with_drug", "Asymptomatic"] <-     c_mat_high_int["without_drug", "Asymptomatic"] + 10000    compare_model_runs(     extractor_fn = get_icer,     comparison_fn = expect_gt,     params_1 = list(state_c_matrix = c_mat_high_int),     params_2 = list(),     data = base_params,     label = "T09: Increasing intervention costs increases ICER"   )    # T10: Costs with standard discount < undiscounted costs   compare_model_runs(     extractor_fn = get_costs,     comparison_fn = expect_lt,     params_1 = list(discount_rate = 0.035),     params_2 = list(discount_rate = 0),     data = base_params,     label = "T10: Discounted less than undiscounted costs"   )    # T11: Set cost discount rate to infinity. Costs equal zero t > 0   res_cycle_zero <- run_model(base_params, n_cycles = 1)   check_model_costs(     data = base_params,     discount_rate = 1000,     expected_costs = get_costs(res_cycle_zero),     tolerance = 0.01,     label = "T11: High discount total costs equal cycle 0 costs"   ) }) #> Test passed with 5 successes 🎊.

title: Custom Expectations and Advanced Testing
code: test_that("Population calculations using life expectancy (LE)", {   t_names <- get_arm_names(base_params)    # T01: Treatment effect the same for all treatments (including no treatment)   no_effect_p_matrix <- base_params$p_matrix   no_effect_p_matrix[, , "with_drug"] <-     no_effect_p_matrix[, , "without_drug"]   res_no_effect <- run_model(base_params, p_matrix = no_effect_p_matrix)    expect_equal(     unname(get_qalys(res_no_effect)["with_drug"]),     unname(get_qalys(res_no_effect)["without_drug"]),     label = "T01: QALYs must be equal when relative treatment effect is 1"   )    expect_equal(     unname(get_le(res_no_effect)["with_drug"]),     unname(get_le(res_no_effect)["without_drug"]),     label = "T01: LEs must be equal when relative treatment effect is 1"   )    # T02: If all transition probabilities to death are 0, LE is n_cycles   n_cycles_test <- 50   no_death_p_matrix <- base_params$p_matrix   no_death_p_matrix[, "Dead", ] <- 0    # Normalise all rows simultaneously   no_death_p_matrix <- prop.table(no_death_p_matrix, margin = c(1, 3))    no_death_p_matrix["Dead", , ] <- 0   no_death_p_matrix["Dead", "Dead", ] <- 1    no_death_p_matrix <- array(     no_death_p_matrix,     dim = dim(base_params$p_matrix),     dimnames = dimnames(base_params$p_matrix)   )    check_model_le_pp(     data = base_params,     p_matrix = no_death_p_matrix,     n_cycles = n_cycles_test,     expected_le = setNames(c(n_cycles_test, n_cycles_test), t_names),     label = "T02: LE should be n_cycles when all p_death=0"   )    # T03: If all transition probabilities to death are 1, LE is 1 cycle   # (LE expectation depends on within-cycle correction implementation)   dead_p_matrix <- base_params$p_matrix   dead_p_matrix[] <- 0   dead_p_matrix[, "Dead", ] <- 1    check_model_le_pp(     data = base_params,     p_matrix = dead_p_matrix,     expected_le = setNames(c(1, 1), t_names),     label = "T03: LE should be 1 when all p_death=1"   ) }) #> Test passed with 4 successes 🌈.

what: 3. Reproducible Stochastic PSA Tests with withr (T12)
title: Custom Expectations and Advanced Testing
text: Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis (PSA) involves random sampling, stochastic tests must set random number generator (RNG) seed reproducible. Rather calling set.seed() globally—permanently alters RNG state subsequent tests—withr package provides withr::with_seed(), sets seed temporarily single code block automatically restores previous RNG state afterward. Test T12 verifies Beta-distributed utility draws generated sample_psa_parameters() remain strictly within (0,1)(0, 1):
code: test_that("T12: PSA beta samples remain within (0, 1)", {   withr::with_seed(42, {     psa_samples <- sample_psa_parameters(       n_sim = 1000,       base_params = base_params     )     beta_cols <- grep("^utility_", names(psa_samples), value = TRUE)     for (col in beta_cols) {       expect_true(         all(psa_samples[[col]] > 0 & psa_samples[[col]] < 1),         label = paste0(           "T12: beta-sampled '", col,           "' must lie strictly in (0, 1)"         )       )     }   }) }) #> Test passed with 2 successes 🎊.

what: 1. Hierarchy of Testing in Health Economic Modelling
title: The HTA Verification Framework
text: Testing can performed different levels abstraction. Adapted software engineering Test Pyramid framework (Cohn, 2009), automated checks health economic modelling organized three structural tiers: Level 1: Unit Testing (Lowest Level — Fast, High Isolation) Isolates smallest testable parts application (“units”)—typically single, self-contained helper function—verifies function correctly (e.g., function converts rate probability, applies discount factor, draws parameter sample). Level 2: Integration Testing (Middle Level — Subcomponent Interaction) Verifies multiple components (input structures, transition matrices, simulation loops, summary extractors) interact correctly produce logically sound results. health economic models frequently lack simple “test oracle” complex multi-state traces, executing run_model() controlled boundary conditions check summary outputs like QALYs, Life Expectancy (LE), ICERs primarily operates integration level. Level 3: System End--End Testing (Highest Level — Full Pipeline) Executes entire decision-analytic pipeline raw data ingestion final policy outputs (e.g., running 10,000-iteration Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis (PSA) pipeline verify completes without memory leaks, handles missing data gracefully, outputs valid ICER CEAC).

what: 2. Why Use testthat Instead of Ad-Hoc Console Checks?
title: The HTA Verification Framework
text: testthat package (Wickham, 2011) standard framework automated testing R. set R package project use testthat (edition 3), run: creates tests/testthat/ directory tests/testthat.R runner script. Automated checks testthat written expectations (functions starting expect_, expect_equal(), expect_lt(), expect_gt(), expect_true()) grouped inside test_that("<description>", { ... }) blocks. title: Validate Cost-Effectiveness and Decision-Analytic Models
text: Automated Verification Unit Testing Health Economic HTA Models R testhta provides practical, software-engineering-inspired framework applying automated verification (unit, integration, system testing) health economic health technology assessment (HTA) models R. Built around testthat package, testhta accompanies tutorial paper “Automated Verification Health Economic Models R: Hands-Tutorial” (Green, Gallardo, & Lamrock, 2026) includes complete 3-state discrete-time cohort Markov model case study verification test suite. Ensuring HTA model quality rely solely ad-hoc console checks manual spreadsheet audits. testhta makes verification automated, reproducible, transparent—proactively catching silent logic bugs influence reimbursement decisions.

title: Validate Cost-Effectiveness and Decision-Analytic Models
text: 🧪 Custom Verification Expectations: High-level wrapper expectations (check_model_qalys(), check_model_costs(), check_model_le(), check_model_le_pp()) verify model outputs expected boundary values. 🔄 Relational Model Comparators: Compare outputs across parameter configurations using compare_model_runs() (e.g., verifying positive discounting reduces future QALYs costs, removing intervention costs reduces ICER). 🔗 Modular Helper Interface: Isolate model internals test scripts using getters (get_qalys(), get_costs(), get_le(), get_le_pp(), get_icer()) pipe-friendly setters (set_discount_rate(), set_time_horizon(), set_costs(), set_utilities(), set_p_matrix()) alongside run_model() wrapper. ⚙️ Executable Case Study & Scaffolding: Includes 3-state (Asymptomatic, Progressive, Dead) cohort Markov model (ce_markov()), baseline parameters (base_params), end--end tutorial test script (inst/tutorial-paper/run-model-tests.R), use_hta_unittests() scaffold test suite project.

what: The HTA Verification Test Registry (T01 – T12)
title: Validate Cost-Effectiveness and Decision-Analytic Models
text: verification checks testhta operationalize established HTA quality-assurance frameworks (McCabe & Dixon, 2000; Tappenden & Chilcott, 2014; Dasbach & Elbasha, 2017; CHEERS) across 12 core test scenarios (T01–T12) grouped four domains: Population Tests (T01–T03): Equal treatment effects yield equal LYGs QALYs (T01); zero mortality yields life expectancy equal time horizon (T02); immediate 100% mortality yields life expectancy 1 cycle (T03). QALY Tests (T04–T07): Zero discount rate living utilities =1= 1 yields total QALYs equal LE (T04); living utilities =1= 1 yields QALY gains equal LYGs (T05); positive discount rate reduces QALYs (T06); infinite/extreme discount rate reduces QALY gains time 0 zero (T07). Cost Tests (T08–T11): Zero intervention cost reduces ICER (T08); increased intervention cost increases ICER (T09); zero vs. positive cost discounting (T10); infinite/extreme cost discount rate reduces costs time 0 zero (T11). Input / PSA Tests (T12): Stochastic parameter samples drawn Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis (PSA) respect distribution domain boundaries (e.g., Beta utility draws strictly (0,1)(0, 1) using withr::with_seed()). complete test matrix, step--step code examples, custom expectations, AI-assisted testing workflows (model-context.md), see package vignettes: - Introduction testhta & Case Study Model - HTA Verification Framework (T01–T12) - R Test Code Examples (Discounting, Costs, Population) - Custom Expectations & Stochastic PSA Testing - Automating Tests & AI-Assisted Verification

title: testhta 0.1.0
text: Added 3-state (Asymptomatic, Progressive, Dead) discrete-time cohort Markov model (ce_markov(), p_matrix_cycle(), sample_psa_parameters()) baseline parameter dataset (base_params, aliased test_data). get_costs() get_costs_pp(): Retrieve total per-person discounted costs. get_icer(), get_incremental_costs(), get_incremental_qalys(): Calculate incremental cost-effectiveness metrics. get_le() get_le_pp(): Retrieve total per-person Life Expectancy. get_qalys() get_qalys_pp(): Retrieve total per-person discounted Quality-Adjusted Life Years. get_arm_names(), get_state_costs(), get_state_utilities(), get_transition_matrix(): Extract parameter-level structures treatment arm. Added use_hta_unittests() automatically generate testthat directory structures pre-configured verification test scripts aligned HTA Verification Registry (T01 – T12). set_costs(): Modify state-occupancy costs. set_discount_rate(): Modify model discount rates. set_p_matrix(): Modify transition probability arrays. set_time_horizon(): Modify simulation time horizon. set_utilities(): Modify state-specific utilities.

title: testhta 0.1.0
text: check_model_costs(): Assert expected costs bounding conditions. check_model_le() check_model_le_pp(): Assert expected total per-person life expectancy bounding conditions. check_model_qalys(): Assert expected QALYs bounding conditions. compare_model_runs(): Assert directional logical relationships two model parameter configurations. run_model(): Core parameter-override wrapper executing underlying Markov engine.

title: testhta 0.1.0
text: Created pkgdown documentation website using Bootstrap 5 flatly Bootswatch theme. introduction: Case study overview, model architecture (“separation concerns”), setters/getters. verification-framework: Software engineering Test Pyramid T01 – T12 HTA Verification Test Registry. basic-tests: Step--step R test code examples discounting (T06, T07, T11), costs (T08), population (T03). validation-guide: Custom expectations (T01 – T11) reproducible stochastic PSA testing withr (T12). automating-hta-unit-tests: Automating test execution, scaffolding use_hta_unittests(), AI-assisted testing (model-context.md).
